name: Separation of powers
description: Legislative, executive, and judicial functions are assigned to distinct branches at the federal level, with checks and balances intended to prevent concentrated power and arbitrary rule.
foundationStrengthRationale: Explicit in Articles I–III; treated as a core structural principle in U.S. constitutional doctrine.

pros.claim: Reduces the risk that a single actor can make, enforce, and interpret law without accountability from other branches.
pros.evidence: Institutional design allocates distinct core functions and inter-branch checks.

cons.claim: Can slow decision-making and invite branch conflict, gridlock, or emergency-power stretching of formal lines.
cons.evidence: Recurring debates over war powers, appointments, and enforcement discretion illustrate friction.
